definitions.explanation: A 12-month period used for accounting and budgeting purposes. In Japan, the fiscal year typically runs from April 1 to March 31.
The annual period during which schools and universities are in session. In Japan, it runs from April to March.

examples.japanese: {今|こん}{年度|ねんど}の{予算|よさん}。
{来|らい}{年度|ねんど}の{予算|よさん}を{作成|さくせい}している。
examples.english: We are preparing next fiscal year's budget.

examples.japanese: 2024{年度|ねんど}の{売上|うりあげ}は{過去|かこ}{最高|さいこう}だった。
examples.english: Sales for fiscal year 2024 were the highest ever.

examples.japanese: {新|しん}{年度|ねんど}が{始|はじ}まる。
{日本|にほん}の{学|がく}{年度|ねんど}は4{月|がつ}に{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: The academic year in Japan starts in April.

examples.japanese: {年度|ねんど}{末|まつ}は3{月|がつ}なので、この{時期|じき}は{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: The end of the fiscal year is in March, so this period is busy.

notes:
{年度|ねんど} refers to an administrative period of one year that may not align with the calendar year. In Japan, both the fiscal year ({会計|かいけい}{年度|ねんど}) and academic year ({学|がく}{年度|ねんど}) run from April to March.

Common expressions:
- {今|こん}{年度|ねんど} (this fiscal/academic year)
- {来|らい}{年度|ねんど} (next fiscal/academic year)
- {前|ぜん}{年度|ねんど} (last fiscal/academic year)
- {年度|ねんど}{末|まつ} (end of fiscal year)
- {年度|ねんど}{初|はじ}め (beginning of fiscal year)

Distinct from {年|ねん} (calendar year) which follows January to December.
